original_question: Determine whether there exists a birack whose induced action on virtual braids is faithful, and determine whether the invariant for virtual braids cited in [150] is faithful. More broadly, decide whether the known linear actions fail precisely because the corresponding linear invariants of virtual knots and links are not faithful.
target_in_paper: Section 8.1, Problem 9 (“Virtual braids”); the second clause is revisited later in Section 8.1, Problem 45.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s virtual-braid faithfulness problem: it asks both for a birack giving a faithful action on virtual braids and for faithfulness of the cited virtual-braid invariant. It also correctly notices the paper’s accompanying remark that linear biquandle actions are not faithful and that this is connected to likely non-faithfulness of the corresponding linear virtual-knot/link invariants.
missing_details: The exact official target is Section 8.1, Problem 9 (“Virtual braids”); your final sentence is not stated there as a separate open problem, but only as an explanatory remark.
The reference number in your draft is wrong: the paper asks about the invariant in [157], not [150]. In this paper, [150] is an unrelated rack-homology reference.

To be stand-alone, the question should specify that a birack is meant in the Section 6.1 sense: a set X with a switch map S: X^2 -> X^2 satisfying invertibility, right invertibility, and the set-theoretic Yang–Baxter equation, but not necessarily the biquandle condition.

If one mentions linear actions, the nearby context defines “linear” using an associative ring R with identity, with X an R-module and switch matrix S = [[A,B],[C,D]] for A, B, C, D in R; the paper does not formulate this over a field.
The ambient braid object should be identified as the virtual braid groups V B_n; Section 8.3 supplies that notation and generators/relations.

The paper’s wording is weaker than your ‘fail precisely because’: it says the non-faithfulness of linear biquandle actions ‘almost certainly means’ the corresponding linear invariants of virtual knots and links are not faithful.
The paper later identifies the invariant more concretely as Manturov’s invariant F for virtual braids (Problem 45), but the nearest official formulation is still Problem 9.
The paper does not add extra hypotheses such as a fixed n, a field, or a special subclass of biracks in Problem 9, so those should not be introduced unless explicitly marked as clarification.
refined_question: Does there exist a birack X in the sense of Section 6.1—i.e. a set with a switch S: X^2 -> X^2 satisfying invertibility, right invertibility, and the set-theoretic Yang–Baxter equation, but not necessarily the biquandle condition—such that the standard switch-induced representations of the virtual braid groups V B_n are faithful; and, specifically, is Manturov’s invariant of virtual braids from [157] (Recognition of virtual braids; see also [6, 115, 169]) faithful as an invariant of virtual braids?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Section 8.1, Problem 9, because its first two questions match that problem almost verbatim. The only major factual mismatch is the citation number: the paper points to [157], not [150]. The third sentence of the draft also comes from the sentence immediately following Problem 9, but the draft strengthens the paper’s cautious remark (‘almost certainly means’) into a sharper causal claim (‘fail precisely because’). Section 6.1 provides the needed definitions of birack and linear biquandle to make the question self-contained, while Problem 45 later confirms that the invariant in question is Manturov’s invariant F for virtual braids.
